summary: Provisioning hang: systemd-network waits indefinitely on usb-ethernet carrier flaps during depot image step
description:
Issue summary:
During depot imaging in staging (us-east), machines with an attached USB-C dock or USB-to-Ethernet adapter sometimes stall at the network bring-up step. systemd-networkd and NetworkManager show repeated carrier state flaps; the provisioning-agent waits on network-online.target and the imaging step times out, leaving devices in a half-imaged state.

Impact:
- ~6% of Ubuntu 22.04 images in the last 48 hours failed to complete in depot-staging-us-east.
- Blocked devices require manual intervention (reboot/detach dock) which delays repairs.
- This affects internal provisioning throughput during high-volume depot windows.

Environment:
- Depot-staging racks in us-east with USB-C docks (Dell WD19) and several USB3-to-RJ45 adapters (AX88179).
- Ubuntu 22.04 base image, kernel 5.19.0-40, NetworkManager 1.46, systemd 253.
- Provisioning agent v1.18.2 running in the imaging container.

Steps to reproduce (intermittent):
1. Attach USB-C dock with onboard Ethernet or plug in USB3-Ethernet adapter.
2. Boot PXE image and start depot imaging job.
3. Provisioning agent waits for network-online.target; logs show repeated carrier on/off events from the USB NIC.
4. After 15-20 minutes the imaging job times out and the host is left at a partial state.

Observed logs and artifacts:
- Journal excerpts (nm and kernel):
  > kernel: usb 3-2: new high-speed USB device number 7 using xhci_hcd
  > kernel: r8152 3-2:1.0 eth0: v1.12.9 driver loaded
  > NetworkManager[1212]: <info>  [03-10 10:22:15] device (eth0): link connected
  > NetworkManager[1212]: <warn>  [03-10 10:22:17] device (eth0): link disconnected
  > systemd[1]: NetworkManager-dispatcher[2321]: Waiting for carrier...
- Provisioning agent log: "waiting for network-online.target: timed out after 900s"
- Kernel dmesg shows occasional USB resets for the adapter.

Hypothesis:
- The USB Ethernet adapter driver (r8152 / ax88179) combined with specific dock firmware is flapping carrier state when traffic/energy-saving interactions occur during PXE/bootstrap, causing NetworkManager to keep retrying and blocking systemd-network-online.
- Provisioning-agent is relying on network-online.target which is too strict for flaky USB NICs; we should either add a shorter fallback or use an alternate reachability probe (e.g., DHCP success/ping to provisioning server).

Initial troubleshooting steps taken:
- Confirmed replication in staging with same dock model and adapter. (Field tech: removed dock = imagening proceeds normally).
- Upgraded provisioning-agent in a test container to v1.18.3 with extra logging; no behavioral change.
- Temporarily adjusted systemd-networkd-wait-online timeout to 30s in a test image; imaging proceeds but we saw post-image network configuration failures in a small fraction of hosts.

Next steps / action items:
- [Assigned] Mateo to capture full packet traces and USB reset timestamps on a repro machine (ETA 2026-03-12).
- [Investigate] Try alternate DHCP client (dhclient) behavior vs NetworkManager to see if link state flaps still block provisioning.
- [Mitigation] Add a provisioning-agent flag to ignore network-online.target and instead wait for DHCP lease + TCP handshake to provisioning backend (short-term workaround).
- [Long-term] SRE/hardware to coordinate with depot vendor to test dock firmware; open support ticket with dock vendor if we can repro consistently.

Requested by: depot support shift lead for March maintenance window.
